source.title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems

accepted.question_text: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one develop an algorithm that computes an inner-outer factorization in the non-standard case? The desired method should work directly for periodic systems rather than only through lifted reductions, and it should be computationally satisfactory for periodic-system settings.

evidence.quote: For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing inner–outer factorisation (in the non-standard case)

accepted.question_text: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one develop an algorithm for Hankel-norm approximation that is numerically reliable and efficient in the periodic setting?

evidence.quote: For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing ... Hankel-norm approximation

accepted.question_text: For arbitrary lifted systems arising from discrete-time periodic models, can one compute a corresponding periodic descriptor-system realization, including cases in which the lifted-system computations yield a non-causal system? In particular, is there a general algorithm that reconstructs a periodic descriptor realization from such arbitrary lifted representations without losing the relevant structure?
accepted.context_brief: Periodic descriptor realization from lifted systems

evidence.quote: For example, if the result is a non-causal system, then apparently there exists even no algorithm to compute the corresponding periodic descriptor system realisation.
For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing ... periodic descriptor system realisation of arbitrary lifted systems

accepted.question_text: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one develop exact or approximate model-matching algorithms for synthesis problems such as controller design, observer design, and fault-detection filter design? The open problem is to obtain effective synthesis methods for these periodic systems within exact or approximate model-matching frameworks.

evidence.quote: For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing ... or for the solution of controller/observer/fault detection filter synthesis problems using exact or approximate model matching approaches.

accepted.question_text: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one design efficient algorithms for solving periodic linear matrix inequalities (LMIs)?

evidence.quote: Moreover, there exist no efficient algorithms to solve periodic linear matrix inequalities (LMIs).

accepted.question_text: For continuous-time linear periodic systems, can one develop algorithms that compute frequency responses efficiently?

evidence.quote: For continuous-time periodic systems, there are no algorithms for efficient computation of frequency responses

accepted.question_text: For continuous-time linear periodic systems, can one develop effective stabilization algorithms that compute stabilizing solutions directly in the periodic setting?

evidence.quote: For continuous-time periodic systems, there are no algorithms for efficient computation of frequency responses, stabilisation or pole assignment.

accepted.question_text: For continuous-time linear periodic systems, can one develop pole-assignment algorithms that assign desired closed-loop poles efficiently and reliably in the periodic setting?

evidence.quote: For continuous-time periodic systems, there are no algorithms for efficient computation of frequency responses, stabilisation or pole assignment.

accepted.question_text: Can one develop new computational methods for solving periodic differential linear matrix inequalities arising in continuous-time periodic systems?

evidence.quote: New methods are also necessary for the solution of periodic differential LMIs.

accepted.question_text: Continuous-time periodic systems are sometimes represented in a frequency-lifted form that produces large structured matrices with block Toeplitz or block Toeplitz-plus-diagonal structure. Can one develop efficient structure-exploiting or structure-preserving algorithms for computations based on this frequency-lifted representation?

evidence.quote: Some of existing computational methods employ the frequency-lifted representation of continuous-time periodic systems ... which leads to large-scale structured system matrices with block Toeplitz or block Toeplitz plus diagonal structures. Efficient structure exploiting/preserving algorithms using this representation are still missing and their development is an open field for research.
